staged_source_snapshot.description: Stage 01 reproduced against this staged vulnerable worktree in the ARVO workspace container. Its line map matches the saved ASan frames (`encoding.c:539`, `readclause.c:174`, `readclause.c:663`) even though sample metadata names vulnerable commit `0fa9737a002cc9c99330f32b650e8804241e7436`; the staged snapshot still contains the same unguarded trailing `c2 = GetC();` hunk that `patch.diff` fixes.

classification.classification_note: AddressSanitizer reports `heap-buffer-overflow READ of size 1` in `string_decoder_getc_utf_8()`. Source analysis shows `ReadClause()` reaches that sink because the `CTRL_EMBEDDED 'B'` branch performs one extra `GetC()` after EOF.

bug_description.original: OSS-Fuzz issue 42512849 (espeak-ng): Heap-buffer-overflow READ 1 found by fuzz target ssml-fuzzer [asan]. https://issues.oss-fuzz.com/issues/42512849
bug_description.original_source: sample_info.json issue_description / patch.diff / sanitizer_trace.txt / reproduction_report.json / staged vulnerable worktree `/src/espeak-ng`
bug_description.normalized: The staged witness is the exact two-byte file `01 42`. The libFuzzer harness copies those bytes into a heap buffer, appends a NUL terminator, and calls `espeak_Synth()` with UTF-8 and SSML-related parsing flags, so the vulnerable parser sees the three-byte string `01 42 00`. In `ReadClause()`, the first byte `0x01` is `CTRL_EMBEDDED`, the second byte `'B'` selects the embedded punctuation-option command, and `if ((c2 = GetC()) == '0')` then consumes the appended NUL terminator in-bounds. That read leaves the decoder at EOF while `c2` is `0`, so the guarded punctuation-list loop `while (!iswspace(c2) && !Eof())` correctly stops immediately. Vulnerable `ReadClause()` still falls through to the trailing `c2 = GetC();` at line 663 without checking `!Eof()`. `GetC()` forwards the exhausted decoder into `string_decoder_getc_utf_8()`, whose first statement dereferences `*decoder->current++` one byte past the 3-byte heap buffer. The staged fix adds the missing `if (!Eof()) c2 = GetC();` guard.

source.description: First project-side materialization of vulnerability-relevant input state. In synchronous synthesis the decoder ignores the explicit `size` argument and recomputes the NUL-terminated witness length from the attacker-controlled heap buffer itself.
source.value_from: The staged `poc` has SHA-256 `abae8bc33fe844e0b33b5fe9ba0a479131e6124034c4d84e2867b4c8ae8b7265` and exact bytes `01 42`. `tests/ssml-fuzzer.c` copies those two bytes into `str`, appends `0x00`, and calls `espeak_Synth(..., size + 1, ...)`; in synchronous mode `espeak_ng_Synthesize()` marks `size` unused at `speech.c:665`, so this helper measures the resulting `01 42 00` string with `strlen(string) + 1` and derives `length == 3`.

sink.description: ASan sink. The UTF-8 decoder dereferences `decoder->current` after `ReadClause()` has already advanced it to `decoder->end`, so the read lands exactly one byte past the `01 42 00` heap buffer.
sink.note: The saved AddressSanitizer report records `heap-buffer-overflow READ of size 1` at `src/libespeak-ng/encoding.c:539:15`, and the faulting address is `0` bytes to the right of the 3-byte region allocated by `tests/ssml-fuzzer.c`.

root_cause.description: Root cause. After the `B`-command parser has already consumed the appended NUL and reached EOF, `ReadClause()` still performs one more character fetch unconditionally instead of checking `!Eof()` first.
root_cause.note: The staged fix in `patch.diff` changes this exact tail to `if (!Eof()) c2 = GetC();`.

tainted_value_origin.description: The harness materializes the exact two-byte witness as a heap string, appends one NUL terminator, and submits the resulting three-byte UTF-8 buffer to espeak-ng with `espeakCHARS_UTF8 | espeakPHONEMES | espeakSSML`.

parser_admitted.description: With `c1 == CTRL_EMBEDDED` and `c2 == 'B'`, the witness is admitted to the embedded punctuation-option parser instead of being handled as ordinary text.

coarse_trace.summary: The synchronous decoder measures the attacker-controlled NUL-terminated string as three bytes and initializes the UTF-8 decoder over `01 42 00`.
The clause reader consumes `0x01` then `'B'`, turning the witness into `CTRL_EMBEDDED` plus the `B` punctuation-option command and entering that embedded-command branch.
The `B` branch reads the appended NUL as its option byte, reaches EOF, and then skips the guarded punctuation-list loop because `!Eof()` is already false.
Despite EOF already being true, vulnerable `ReadClause()` issues one more `GetC()` at line 663, and `GetC()` forwards the exhausted decoder to the UTF-8 backend without its own EOF guard.
The UTF-8 decoder dereferences `decoder->current` exactly at `decoder->end`, producing the saved 1-byte heap-buffer-overflow read.

fine_trace.note: Source. `text_decoder_decode_string_multibyte()` reaches this helper with `length < 0`, so synchronous synthesis measures the attacker-controlled NUL-terminated witness itself. For the saved `01 42 00` string, `length` becomes `3`.

The helper selects the UTF-8 getter and initializes the decoder over the exact three-byte range `[string, string + 3)`: control byte `0x01`, command letter `'B'`, and the appended NUL terminator. Later EOF checks compare `decoder->current` against this `decoder->end` pointer.
`ReadClause()` fetches the first byte from the decoder into lookahead `c2`. On this witness that byte is `0x01`, i.e. `CTRL_EMBEDDED`, and the decoder advances to the `'B'` byte.

At the top of the first loop iteration, the previous lookahead becomes `c1 == CTRL_EMBEDDED`. The same iteration then executes line 548 to read the second witness byte into `c2`, producing `c2 == 'B'`; the line-550 EOF fallback does not fire because the appended NUL is still unread.
Because `c1 == CTRL_EMBEDDED` and lookahead `c2 == 'B'`, `ReadClause()` enters the embedded punctuation-option command parser rather than treating the bytes as ordinary text.

The `B` branch reads its option byte with `GetC()`. For the exact `01 42 00` string this consumes the appended NUL terminator, sets `c2` to `0`, and advances the decoder to `decoder->end`. Because `c2` is neither `'0'` nor `'1'`, control falls into the custom punctuation-list case with EOF already true.

This loop is the present EOF guard inside the `B<punct list>` parser. With `c2 == 0` from step 6 and EOF already true, the loop is skipped immediately, no punctuation-list bytes are consumed, and execution falls through with the decoder still exhausted.

Root-cause step. Even after step 7 has already established EOF and avoided any list reads, `ReadClause()` still performs one more unconditional fetch. The staged patch fixes this exact site by guarding the call with `if (!Eof())`.
`GetC()` has no separate EOF guard once it is called. The exhausted decoder from step 8 is forwarded directly to the active UTF-8 backend through `text_decoder_getc(p_decoder)`.

Sink. Because steps 6 through 9 reach the UTF-8 backend with `decoder->current == decoder->end`, this dereference reads one byte past the 3-byte `01 42 00` heap buffer, exactly as reported by the saved ASan trace.

allocation_context.note: ASan reports the invalid read is `0` bytes to the right of the 3-byte heap region allocated here for the `01 42 00` string.

sanitizer_ground_truth.patch_resolves_note: The staged patch adds `if (!Eof()) c2 = GetC();` at the exact tail of the `CTRL_EMBEDDED 'B'` parser, so the branch no longer performs a post-EOF fetch after consuming the appended terminator. Stage 02 did not execute the fixed image.
sanitizer_ground_truth.source: staged sanitizer_trace.txt, default_crash_trace.txt, reproduction_report.json, exact staged vulnerable source, patch.diff, and the running Stage 01 workspace container; `run_flags.json` kept runtime disambiguation disabled

cross_validation.root_cause_matches_allocation_context: Yes. ASan's 3-byte heap region is the harness-allocated `01 42 00` string, and the traced root cause is the later missing EOF guard that advances the same buffer's decoder one byte past its end before line 539 dereferences it.

poc.trigger: Stage 01 reproduced the issue by running `PYTHONPATH=gt_generation python3 -m gt_toolkit arvo-workspace --result-dir /mnt/datastore/gt_generation/gt_results/arvo_42512849 run --version vulnerable --expect crash`, which reported `AddressSanitizer: heap-buffer-overflow` at `src/libespeak-ng/encoding.c:539` while `ssml-fuzzer` processed this exact file.

format.name: raw espeak-ng embedded-command witness
format.contract: Exactly the two-byte file stored at `gt_results/arvo_42512849/poc`: `01 42`. The harness appends one NUL byte, so the vulnerable parser sees `01 42 00` with `0x01 == CTRL_EMBEDDED` and `'B'` selecting the embedded punctuation-option command. There are no bytes after the command letter before the appended terminator, so the `B` parser consumes `0x00` as its option byte, reaches EOF, skips the guarded punctuation-list loop, and then executes the unguarded trailing `GetC()`. The staged artifacts do not prove broader trigger classes beyond this exact witness.
